terms.term: FIRST TERM — Myself, My Family & My School

cells.Topic: MYSELF: MY NAME, MY AGE AND MY BODY
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • My full name, my nickname and how to say them clearly / • My age, my birthday, boy/girl; 'I am special' / • Naming body parts: head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, hands, legs / • Senses: I see with my eyes, hear with my ears, smell with my nose / • Song/rhyme: 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes'; 'I am special, I am me'

cells.Topic: MY FAMILY: MEMBERS AND THEIR ROLES
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Members of my family: father, mother, brothers, sisters / • Extended family: grandpa, grandma, uncles, aunts, cousins / • What each member does at home; love and respect for family / • Family song: 'This is my family'; drawing my family / • Saying 'please', 'thank you' and 'sorry' at home

cells.Topic: MY SCHOOL: PLACES, PEOPLE AND THINGS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • My school's name and my class name / • Places in the school: classroom, playground, library, toilet, office / • People in the school: head teacher, teachers, caretaker, school nurse / • My school bag and its contents; taking care of school things / • School tour and matching pictures to places

• Objects in the classroom: table, chair, board, books, pencils, crayons / • Classroom rules: raise your hand, listen, share, keep quiet / • Keeping the classroom clean: dustbin, tidy desks / • Colours of classroom objects (red, blue, yellow, green, black, white) / • Game: 'Find something that is red / round / soft'

• Rooms in my house: sitting room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom / • People who live with me; where I sleep and eat / • My street/village/town; what I see on my way to school / • Near and far, up and down; my home is my first school / • Drawing/talk: 'My house'; role-play home activities

cells.Topic: COLOURS, SHAPES AND SIZES AROUND ME
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Primary colours: red, blue, yellow; black, white, green / • Shapes: circle, square, triangle, star; things of each shape / • Big and small, long and short, tall and short / • Colours in the Nigerian flag (green and white) — first look / • Play: shape hunt, colour sorting, size stacking games
• Rest and relaxation; holiday practice: name my family, sing school songs

• Domestic animals: dog, cat, goat, chicken, cow; their sounds / • Wild animals seen in pictures/stories: lion, elephant, monkey, snake / • Birds: parrot, pigeon, hen, eagle (our national bird — first look) / • Where animals live: home, farm, bush, water, sky / • Songs and actions: 'Old MacDonald', animal-sound games

cells.Topic: GOOD HABITS: GREETINGS, POLITENESS AND CLEANLINESS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Morning, afternoon and evening greetings; greeting elders / • Magic words: please, thank you, sorry, excuse me / • Washing hands before eating and after the toilet / • Brushing teeth morning and night; bathing daily; neat uniform / • Role-play: greeting visitors; Good-Habit Songs and charts
• Review of Weeks 1–9 with songs, pictures, flashcards and games
• Oral, observation and picture-based assessment of all topics learned
• Report cards, awards for participation, holiday practice: greet everyone politely

terms.term: SECOND TERM — My Community & My Country — Nigeria

cells.Topic: PEOPLE IN MY COMMUNITY: OUR HELPERS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Helpers: doctor, nurse, teacher, police officer, firefighter, tailor, farmer / • What each helper does; why they are important / • Where each helper works (hospital, school, police station, farm) / • Saying thank you to helpers; community helpers song / • Visit/role-play: a helper visits the class

• My country's name: Nigeria; I am a Nigerian / • The Nigerian flag: green-white-green; what the colours mean (first idea) / • Nigeria on a simple map/picture: 'our country is big' / • Our currency: Naira — coins and notes (first look) / • Song: 'One Nigeria'; colouring the flag green and white

• Foods we eat: rice, yam, beans, plantain, fruits; Nigerian dishes / • Clothes we wear: traditional and everyday, e.g. Ankara, lace, agbada / • Festivals we celebrate: Christmas, Eid (Sallah), New Year, birthdays / • Music and dance at festivals; sharing food with neighbours / • Show-and-tell: my favourite food, my festival clothes

• Sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy days; hot and cold / • Rainy season and dry season in Nigeria / • Clothes for different weather: umbrella, sweater, cap / • The harmattan: dusty, hazy and cool mornings / • Weather chart in class; songs about the sun and rain

• Trees, flowers, grass and vegetables in my environment / • Parts of a plant: root, stem, leaf, flower (simple) / • Fruits and vegetables I eat: orange, mango, banana, tomato, pepper / • Plants give us food, shade and fresh air; watering plants / • Planting a seed in class and watching it grow

• The five senses and their organs (seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching) / • Safety at home: fire, hot water, sharp objects, medicines / • Road safety: hold an adult's hand, look before crossing / • Stranger danger: never follow strangers, never take gifts from strangers / • Safety songs, posters and 'safe vs unsafe' picture games
• Rest and relaxation; holiday practice: name three community helpers

cells.Topic: NIGERIAN ANIMALS, BIRDS AND THEIR HOMES
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Farm animals in Nigeria and their uses: goat, cow, chicken, sheep / • Animals and their homes: dog-kennel, chicken-coop, cow-shed / • The eagle: our national bird; the lion: the 'king of animals' / • Animals in stories: tortoise, rabbit, lion (folktales) / • Picture matching: animal to home, animal to sound

cells.Topic: SONGS, RHYMES AND STORIES OF NIGERIA
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Nursery rhymes and Nigerian lullabies and folk songs / • Folktales: the tortoise and the wisdom of the world; why the lizard... / • Tales that teach: honesty, sharing, obedience, hard work / • Songs about Nigeria: 'Arise, O Compatriots' (melody, simple) — first listening / • Storytelling circle: pupils retell a story in their own words
• Review of Weeks 1–9 with songs, pictures, games and role-play
• Oral, picture-based and observation assessment of all topics learned
• Report cards, awards, holiday practice: draw the Nigerian flag, greet elders

terms.term: THIRD TERM — My Big World & My Country's Story

cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • The Nok: earliest known civilisation in Nigeria (terra cotta, iron, c. 1500 BC–AD 200) / • Ife and Benin: bronze and terracotta art; Benin walls and bronzes; Obas / • Old Oyo Empire: strong cavalry; Alaafin; Yoruba power / • Kanem-Bornu: by Lake Chad; Mai rulers; trans-Saharan trade / • Sokoto Caliphate: Usman dan Fodio (1804); Jihad; Fulani rule; emirs

cells.Topic: NIGERIAN HISTORY IV: FROM COLONY TO REPUBLIC
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • 1885–1900: the scramble for Africa; British conquests and protectorates / • 1914: amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria (Lord Lugard; name coined) / • 1960: independence from Britain (1 October); 1963: Nigeria became a Republic (Azikiwe first President) / • Nationalist movements: Zik, Awolowo, Bello, Balewa, Macaulay, Aminu Kano / • Timeline mastery: 1861, 1914, 1960, 1963 — drawing dates on a timeline

cells.Topic: NIGERIAN HISTORY V: THE NATION TODAY
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • 1966: first military coup and military rule; 1967–1970: the civil war — Nigeria stayed one / • 1976: Abuja chosen as the new capital; 1991: Abuja became the capital / • 1999: return to democracy; 2023: peaceful handover to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (current) / • Nigeria today: 36 states + FCT, 774 LGAs, over 200 million people — Africa's largest population / • Discussion: unity in diversity — 'One Nigeria, many peoples'

cells.Topic: GEOGRAPHY OF NIGERIA: RIVERS, LANDMARKS AND PLACES
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • River Niger (third-longest in Africa) and River Benue; their confluence at Lokoja / • Other rivers: Kaduna, Sokoto, Gongola, Ogun, Cross River; Niger Delta — Africa's largest delta / • Landmarks: Aso Rock (Abuja), Zuma Rock (Niger State), Olumo Rock (Abeokuta), Obudu Hills / • West Africa's highest point: Chappal Waddi (Mambilla Plateau, Taraba, 2,419 m) / • Map work: rivers and landmarks on the map of Nigeria

cells.Topic: NIGERIA'S ECONOMY: OIL, AGRICULTURE AND RESOURCES
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Petroleum: crude oil — Nigeria's main export; OPEC member since 1971 / • Agriculture: still employs many Nigerians; crops: cocoa, palm oil, groundnut, rubber, cashew / • Other resources: natural gas, tin, coal, limestone, gold, columbite / • Industries: manufacturing, banking, telecoms, film (Nollywood), music (Afrobeats) / • Activity: 'made in Nigeria' — identify 10 Nigerian products

cells.Topic: MAP READING BASICS: NIGERIA AND HER NEIGHBOURS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Map tools: title, key/legend, compass direction (N, S, E, W), scale (idea) / • Directions with the compass: find north on maps of Nigeria / • Neighbours: Benin (west), Niger (north), Chad (north-east, via Lake Chad), Cameroon (east) / • The Gulf of Guinea: Nigeria's coastline to the south (Atlantic Ocean) / • Practical: draw a simple map of your classroom, your street, then Nigeria
• Rest and relaxation; mid-term test on Weeks 1–6

• Africa: 54 countries; second-largest continent; the Nile (longest river) and the Sahara (largest hot desert) / • Landmarks: Mount Kilimanjaro (Tanzania, Africa's highest), Victoria Falls, the Great Rift Valley, the Congo rainforest / • Regions: North, West, East, Central, Southern Africa; the Sahel / • African institutions: AU (African Union, HQ Addis Ababa); ECOWAS (HQ Abuja); AfCFTA (trade) / • Map work: label Africa's regions, rivers and landmarks

cells.Topic: THE WORLD'S NATURAL WONDERS AND FAMOUS PLACES
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Seven natural wonders idea: Grand Canyon, Great Barrier Reef, Mount Everest, Northern Lights, Victoria Falls, Rio's harbour, Paricutín volcano — know a few well / • The deepest trench: Mariana Trench (Pacific); the highest mountain: Everest (8,849 m) / • The Amazon: largest rainforest; the largest river by volume / • Great structures: Great Wall of China, Pyramids of Egypt, Eiffel Tower, Statue of Liberty / • Project: 'Wonders of the World' picture book; world map pin-up
• Review of Weeks 1–9: kingdoms, republic, geography, economy, Africa, wonders
• Term examination: objective questions; map labelling included
• Report cards, awards; holiday practice: draw the map of Nigeria and label 10 states

terms.term: THIRD TERM — World Knowledge, Reasoning & Exam Readiness

cells.Topic: THE SOLAR SYSTEM AND THE EARTH
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • The Solar System: the Sun and eight planets (order facts) / • Earth: third planet; only known world with life; day/night and the seasons (simple) / • Space exploration: first satellite (Sputnik 1, 1957); first human in space (Yuri Gagarin, 1961); first Moon landing (Neil Armstrong, 1969) / • Nigeria in space: NASRDA (National Space Research and Development Agency); NigeriaSat-1, Nigeria's first satellite (2003) / • Craft and quiz: model solar system; planet facts game

cells.Topic: GREAT SCIENTISTS, INVENTORS AND NIGERIAN BRAINS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Inventors and what they gave us: printing press (Gutenberg), telephone (Bell), light bulb (Edison), aeroplane (Wright brothers), penicillin (Fleming), computer (Babbage/Turing idea), internet/web (Berners-Lee) / • Nigerian innovators: Philip Emeagwali (supercomputing), Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (WTO Director-General — first African woman) / • African Nobel winners: Wole Soyinka (Literature, 1986), Kofi Annan (UN, Ghanaian) / • Science facts every pupil should know: water boils at 100°C; plants make food by photosynthesis (idea) / • Research: 'one invention, one inventor' mini-presentations

• UN (United Nations): HQ New York; keeps world peace; 193 member countries; founded 1945 / • UN agencies: UNICEF (children), WHO (health), UNESCO (education/culture), FAO (food/agriculture) / • AU (African Union): HQ Addis Ababa — Africa's unity body; ECOWAS: HQ Abuja — West African body (ECOWAS Chair and summits = current affairs) / • Other bodies: OPEC (HQ Vienna — oil), FIFA (HQ Zurich — football), CAF (HQ Cairo — African football), Commonwealth (London) / • Quiz: match organisation to its job and headquarters

cells.Topic: SPORTS I: NIGERIAN SPORTS HEROES AND HISTORY
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Football heroes: the Super Eagles (AFCON champions 1994, 2013); players: Kanu, Okocha, Osimhen, Mikel / • The Super Falcons: record 11-time African champions; the D'Tigress (basketball) and Golden Eaglets (U-17 world champions 5 times) / • Athletics heroes: Chioma Ajunwa (Olympic gold, 1996); Tobi Amusan (100m hurdles world champion and world record, 2022); Blessing Okoagbare / • Boxing and others: Anthony Joshua (British-Nigerian champions idea); Nigeria at the Olympics (first medal 1964) / • Project: 'My Sporting Hero' poster; inter-house quiz on Nigerian sport

cells.Topic: SPORTS II: WORLD SPORTS AND COMPETITIONS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • The Olympic Games: every 4 years; summer and winter; the five rings symbol; motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius / • The FIFA World Cup: every 4 years; the biggest football competition (see appendix for 2026 result) / • The Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON): Africa's football trophy; the Nations Cup in athletics and the Commonwealth Games / • Other sports: athletics, swimming, basketball, table tennis, lawn tennis, boxing, chess (sportsmanship!) / • Current affairs in sport: latest champions (refresh yearly — see appendix)

cells.Topic: CURRENT AFFAIRS II: NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL NEWS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • What happened in Nigeria this term: government, education, economy, security (guided by teacher) / • Africa and the world in the news: AU summits, ECOWAS, UN activities / • Weather and environment news: climate (idea), flooding, hot seasons / • Technology news: phones, computers, artificial intelligence (idea), the internet / • News journal: each pupil keeps a 'Current Affairs Notebook' — 2 items a week
• Rest and relaxation; mid-term test on Weeks 1–6

cells.Topic: VERBAL AND QUANTITATIVE REASONING: PATTERNS AND LOGIC
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Why reasoning is in the entrance exam: it tests thinking, not memory / • Verbal: odd one out, word meanings, opposites, analogy (book:read, knife:cut) / • Quantitative: number series, missing numbers, simple sequences, comparison / • Picture/spatial: patterns, mirror images, counting shapes (simple) / • Practice drills: 10 reasoning questions weekly; timing games

• Full mock paper in entrance-exam format: 60 questions, 60 marks, timed / • Sections: Nigeria GK · Current Affairs · Social Studies · Basic Science · History & Geography · Reasoning / • Marking, error analysis and class review of the top 10 missed questions / • Exam techniques: read carefully, answer all, manage time, no cheating / • Parent brief: how to support exam revision at home
• Comprehensive revision: all pillars, all terms; mixed drills and quizzes
• Year examination: entrance-exam style objective paper
• Promotion ceremony; GK awards; holiday practice: daily news + one atlas page

terms.term: FIRST TERM — Deep Civics: Structure, Democracy and Institutions

cells.Topic: THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF NIGERIA: A COMPLETE PICTURE
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Nigeria: a Federal Republic — federal, state and local governments / • 36 states + FCT (Abuja); 774 LGAs; six geopolitical zones (full recall) / • Population: over 200 million — the most populous black nation; Africa's largest economy idea / • National symbols full set: flag, coat of arms, anthem, pledge, motto, colours, currency / • Speed tests: states-and-capitals in 5 minutes; map labelling of all zones

• The 1999 Constitution (as amended): the supreme law of Nigeria / • Key principles: democracy, rule of law, separation of powers, federalism / • Fundamental objectives and directive principles (simple idea) / • Citizenship by birth and by registration (simple); dual citizenship idea / • Discussion: why the constitution protects every Nigerian

• Democracy: government of the people, by the people, for the people / • Elections: voters choose leaders; INEC organises them; free and fair idea / • The electoral cycle: registration, campaigns, voting, results, swearing in / • Voting age: 18; the 2027 general elections (current affairs — verify yearly) / • Role-play: full class election — register, campaign, vote, count

cells.Topic: NATIONAL INSTITUTIONS II: AGENCIES AND ACRONYMS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Security: Police (NPF), Army, Navy, Air Force; DSS; NSCDC; customs; FRSC — road safety / • Anti-corruption: EFCC (Economic and Financial Crimes Commission), ICPC / • Standards and consumers: SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria), NAFDAC (food and drugs) / • Identity and data: NIMC (NIN), NPC (census), NCC (communications), NIPOST (postal) / • Acronym drill: 20 agencies — full name + one job each

cells.Topic: NIGERIA AND THE WORLD: DIPLOMACY AND MISSIONS
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Foreign relations: Nigeria's embassies abroad and foreign embassies in Abuja / • Nigeria in world bodies: UN, AU, ECOWAS, OPEC, Commonwealth, Islamic Cooperation (idea) / • Nigeria's role: peacekeeping in Africa; 'Giant of Africa' idea / • Pan-Africanism: Africa's unity movement; AfCFTA (African free trade area) / • Current affairs: one world meeting Nigeria attended this term

• Courts and their work: customary/area courts, magistrates, high courts, Court of Appeal, Supreme Court (final) / • The Chief Justice of Nigeria: the head of the judiciary (current: Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun) / • Judges: impartial umpires; fair hearing for all; presumption of innocence / • Criminal vs civil matters (simple idea); punishment and correction vs revenge / • Mock trial in class: 'The Case of the Missing Book'
• Rest and relaxation; mid-term test on Weeks 1–6

• Nationalism: love and loyalty to one's country; patriotism in daily life / • National integration: unity in diversity; the 'Nigerian spirit' / • How children show patriotism: obeying laws, being honest, respecting the flag and anthem, working hard / • Explaining the National Pledge line by line; the anthem's meaning / • Essay/poem: 'What I will do for Nigeria'

• Human rights: rights every person has simply by being human / • The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) and Nigeria's Child Rights Act (2003): survival, protection, development, participation / • Child rights: education, health, play, protection from abuse and child labour / • Child duties: respect parents and teachers, study, help at home, be good citizens / • Discussion: rights vs responsibilities; scenarios of rights being protected or violated
• Review of Weeks 1–9: federation, constitution, elections, institutions, rights
• Term examination: full objective paper on civics, institutions and rights
• Report cards, awards; holiday practice: current affairs notebook for the holidays

terms.term: SECOND TERM — History, Geography and the World Economy

cells.Topic: NIGERIAN HISTORY VI: THE COMPLETE TIMELINE
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Key dates: 1861 (Lagos annexed) · 1914 (amalgamation) · 1946–57 steps to self-rule · 1960 (independence) · 1963 (republic) · 1967–70 (civil war) · 1976 (Abuja chosen) · 1991 (Abuja capital) · 1999 (democracy) · 2015 · 2023 (current era) / • Ordering events: put major events on a timeline in sequence / • Independence celebrations: 1 October 2026 = Nigeria at 66 / • Memory work: 'dates that made Nigeria' — 10 key dates / • Timeline project: a wall chart of Nigerian history

cells.Topic: MILITARY AND CIVILIAN RULE; DEMOCRACY REBORN
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • 1966–1999: military coups and military governments (idea: interruptions to democracy) / • 1999: the Fourth Republic began; elections since 1999 (1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023) / • Growth of democracy: peaceful transfers of power; the 2015 opposition victory as a major step / • The 2023 election and the current administration (current affairs — verify yearly) / • Debate: 'Is democracy better for Nigeria?' (class discussion, balanced)

cells.Topic: NIGERIA'S ECONOMY: OIL, TRADE AND THE FUTURE
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Crude oil and gas: the backbone of exports; OPEC membership; fuel and the refineries (idea) / • Diversification: agriculture, manufacturing, services, digital economy (fintech, tech start-ups) / • The naira, the CBN, and the value of money; inflation (simple idea) / • Trade: exports (oil, cocoa, cashew, sesame) and imports; ports and borders / • Economic current affairs: prices, budgets, taxes (light-touch, teacher-guided)

• Rivers: Niger, Benue, Kaduna, Sokoto, Gongola, Cross, Ogun, Osun; the Niger Delta / • Highlands and plains: Jos Plateau, Mambilla Plateau (Chappal Waddi — highest), Adamawa / • Cities: Lagos (largest), Abuja (capital), Kano, Ibadan, Port Harcourt, Enugu, Kaduna, Benin City / • Climate zones: rainforest, savannah, Sahel; vegetation and farming / • Mastery test: label 20 features on a blank map of Nigeria

• Continents, oceans, seas and major rivers (Nile, Amazon, Mississippi, Niger, Congo) / • Mountains: Everest (highest), Kilimanjaro (Africa); deserts: Sahara (largest hot), Kalahari, Arabian / • Seas and lakes: Mediterranean, Caspian (largest lake), Lake Chad, Lake Victoria (Africa's largest) / • Countries and capitals: 30 must-know capitals (Africa + world) — full mastery / • Map race: locate any named country in under 15 seconds

cells.Topic: DISCOVERIES AND INVENTIONS THAT CHANGED THE WORLD
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Communication: speech → writing → printing press → telegraph → telephone → radio → TV → internet → mobile → smartphones / • Transport: wheel, sail, steam engine, railway, car, aeroplane, rocket, space station / • Medicine: vaccines (idea), penicillin, malaria treatment; clean water saves lives / • Energy: fire, wood, coal, oil, wind, solar; electricity and the national grid / • Essay: 'The invention I cannot live without'
• Rest and relaxation; mid-term test on Weeks 1–6

cells.Topic: IMPORTANT DAYS: NIGERIA AND THE WORLD (MASTERY)
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Nigeria: 1 Oct Independence · 12 June Democracy Day · 27 May Children's Day · 15 Jan Armed Forces Remembrance · 1 May Workers' Day / • World: 1 Jan New Year · 8 Mar Women's Day · 22 Apr Earth Day · 25 May Africa Day · 5 Jun Environment Day · 20 Nov World Children's Day · 10 Dec Human Rights Day / • Religious and cultural: Christmas, Easter, Eid-el-Fitr, Eid-el-Kabir, New Yam, Durbar / • Why dates matter in exams: date + event + reason / • Calendar project: the class 'Year of Important Days' wall calendar

• Nigeria's resources: oil, gas, coal, tin, limestone, gold, columbite; forest and fisheries / • Environmental problems: deforestation, flooding, erosion, pollution (air, water, land), desertification / • Climate change (idea): global warming, greenhouse gases, rising seas; what children can do / • Conservation: protected areas — Yankari Game Reserve, Cross River National Park, Gashaka-Gumti (Nigeria's largest) / • Action project: class 'Green School' campaign — trees, waste sorting, water saving
• Review of Weeks 1–9: timelines, economy, geography mastery, inventions, days
• Term examination: geography, history and economy objective paper
• Report cards, awards; holiday practice: world map labelling challenge

cells.Topic: CURRENT AFFAIRS IV: SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Nigeria's digital economy: fintech (banking on phones), the National Digital Economy policy idea / • New technologies: artificial intelligence (AI), smartphones, social media, drones — what they are (simple) / • Cyber safety for pupils: strong passwords, no stranger chats, report bad content, screen balance / • Nigeria in tech news (verify yearly, e.g. the 2026 Executive Order on virtual assets coordination) / • Science in the news: health campaigns (e.g. malaria, polio eradication), weather and flooding alerts

cells.Topic: VERBAL AND QUANTITATIVE REASONING: EXAM DRILL
cells.Breakdown (Subtopics) — Areas of Concent: • Verbal reasoning types: synonyms/antonyms, odd one out, analogies, coding/decoding, letter series, sentence completion / • Quantitative types: number series, missing operations, fractions quick facts, percentages (10% = 1/10), simple ratios / • Data and figures: averages idea, reading tables and simple charts / • Speed and accuracy drills: 20 questions in 20 minutes, weekly / • Review of common errors; smarter guessing (eliminate, then choose)
